description: Tasks template for modernization plan. Generate this file alongside plan.md to track individual migration tasks.

tasks.description: Upgrade the application runtime from Java 8 / Spring Boot 2.7.18 to Java 25 / Spring Boot 4.x, including Spring Framework 7.x and Jakarta EE migration (javax.* to jakarta.*).
tasks.reason: The playbook targets Java 25 and Spring Boot 4.x. Java 8, 11, and 17 are end-of-life for internal use. Spring Boot 2.x must be upgraded per charter constraints. This upgrade is a prerequisite for all subsequent Azure service migrations.
tasks.requirements: Upgrade Java to version 25, Spring Boot to 4.x, and Spring Framework to 7.x. Migrate all javax.* imports to jakarta.* equivalents. Update pom.xml parent, properties, and any incompatible dependency versions. Ensure the project compiles and tests pass after the upgrade.

tasks.description: Migrate AMQP messaging from RabbitMQ to Azure Service Bus using Spring Messaging so the application sends and receives messages through a managed Azure service.
tasks.reason: The application currently uses RabbitMQ (Spring AMQP) with hardcoded credentials. The playbook mandates Azure Service Bus as the target messaging service. Managed Identity must be used for authentication.
tasks.requirements: Replace the Spring AMQP / RabbitMQ starter with Spring Cloud Azure Service Bus. Migrate all message producers (RabbitTemplate.convertAndSend) and consumers to Azure Service Bus equivalents. Replace RabbitMQ queue declarations in AppConfig with Service Bus queue/topic configuration. Use Managed Identity for authentication — remove hardcoded RabbitMQ host/port/username/password from application.yml. Map the three existing queues (order.created, inventory.alert, approval.pending) to equivalent Service Bus entities.

tasks.description: Replace password-based MySQL authentication with Azure Managed Identity so the application connects to Azure Database for MySQL without storing credentials.
tasks.reason: The application uses hardcoded MySQL credentials (username: root, password: root) which violates the playbook's secrets management policy. Azure Managed Identity provides credential-free, secure database access.
tasks.requirements: Replace the password-based MySQL datasource configuration with Azure Managed Identity authentication for Azure Database for MySQL. Update Spring Cloud Azure dependencies to support passwordless MySQL authentication. Remove hardcoded datasource username/password from application.yml. Ensure the JDBC URL targets Azure Database for MySQL. Use the Azure MySQL authentication plugin via Managed Identity.

tasks.description: Move all remaining hardcoded credentials and sensitive values from source code and configuration files to Azure Key Vault.
tasks.reason: The application has hardcoded database and RabbitMQ credentials in application.yml. The playbook requires all sensitive values (credentials, API keys, connection strings) to be stored in Azure Key Vault and accessed via the Spring Cloud Azure Key Vault starter or Managed Identity.
tasks.requirements: Identify all hardcoded credentials, API keys, and sensitive configuration values in application.yml and source code. Migrate these values to Azure Key Vault secrets. Configure the Spring Cloud Azure Key Vault starter to retrieve secrets at runtime via Managed Identity. Ensure no plaintext credentials remain in application.yml, application.properties, environment variables, or source code.

tasks.description: Replace RestTemplate with the ServiceMesh SDK (com.acme.mesh.ServiceMesh) for all service-to-service HTTP communication.
tasks.reason: RestTemplate is prohibited by the playbook guardrails because it bypasses the mesh layer. The ServiceMesh SDK provides automatic circuit breaking, mTLS termination, distributed tracing, and canary routing. The current code has a RestTemplate bean in AppConfig and RestTemplate usage in VendorService.
tasks.requirements: Remove the RestTemplate bean from AppConfig. Replace all RestTemplate usages in VendorService (and any other classes) with the ServiceMesh SDK (com.acme.mesh.ServiceMesh). Add the ServiceMesh SDK dependency to pom.xml. Ensure all service-to-service HTTP calls route through the ServiceMesh SDK.

tasks.description: Replace SLF4J / @Slf4j logging with InternalLogger (com.acme.logging.InternalLogger) across all application classes.
tasks.reason: SLF4J, Log4j, Logback, and java.util.logging are prohibited by the playbook because they lack trace context integration. InternalLogger injects trace IDs, team tags, and structured JSON, and is the sole approved logging framework.
tasks.requirements: Remove the @Slf4j annotation and all SLF4J imports from InventoryService, PurchaseOrderService, VendorService, and any other classes using SLF4J. Replace with InternalLogger (com.acme.logging.InternalLogger). Add the InternalLogger dependency to pom.xml. Ensure all log statements use InternalLogger APIs. Remove any Logback or SLF4J configuration files.

tasks.description: Replace exception-based flow control with the Result<T> pattern (com.acme.commons.Result) across all service and controller classes.
tasks.reason: Throwing exceptions for business logic flow control and using try/catch blocks for flow control are prohibited by the P0-2024-0847 post-incident mandate. The Result<T> pattern is the approved mechanism for error handling and must be used for all application-level control flow.
tasks.requirements: Identify all places where exceptions are thrown for business logic (e.g., RuntimeException, IllegalArgumentException, IllegalStateException in service methods) and where try/catch is used for flow control. Replace these with the Result<T> pattern from com.acme.commons.Result. Update controller response handling to work with Result<T> return types. Add the com.acme.commons.Result dependency to pom.xml. Remove @ControllerAdvice global exception handlers for business exceptions if present.

tasks.description: Create or update the Dockerfile to containerize the application using the JDK 25 distroless runtime image for Azure Container Apps deployment.
tasks.reason: Azure Container Apps requires a container image. The playbook targets mcr.microsoft.com/openjdk/jdk:25-distroless as the runtime base image and mcr.microsoft.com/openjdk/jdk:25-ubuntu as the build stage image.
tasks.requirements: Create a multi-stage Dockerfile using mcr.microsoft.com/openjdk/jdk:25-ubuntu as the build stage and mcr.microsoft.com/openjdk/jdk:25-distroless as the runtime stage. The build stage should run Maven to produce the application JAR. The runtime stage should copy only the JAR. Expose port 8080. Ensure the Dockerfile is optimised for layer caching.

tasks.description: Deploy the containerized SupplyChain Backend to Azure Container Apps using Bicep infrastructure as code.
tasks.reason: The playbook mandates Azure Container Apps (ACA) as the default compute platform for all Java services in the supply chain system. Deployment must use Managed Identity for all Azure service connections.
tasks.requirements: Generate Bicep IaC to provision an Azure Container Apps environment, Azure Container Registry, Azure Service Bus namespace, Azure Database for MySQL, and Azure Key Vault. Configure Managed Identity for the container app to access all dependent services. Deploy the container image built from the Dockerfile. Expose the application on port 8080.
